name: MCA Denver
funding: Expenses $79.7M (FY2025, incl. capital); SCFD sales tax, City of Denver, Anschutz and Hamilton gifts.
watch: Board list not published online. Liberty Global is telecom and media money.
why_flagged: Board list not published online. Liberty Global is telecom and media money.
records_note: It posts annual reports covering FY17 to FY24, each with donors by gift level, a board list in the report, and Form 990s on ProPublica.

name: McNay Art Museum
funding: FY2025 (year to June): endowment draw $2.15M (20% of $10.7M expenses), contributions $2.25M, memberships $0.56M, admissions $0.29M. No donor list found.
watch: Marion Koogler McNay's oil-wealth bequest (1950) is now a diversified endowment; its draw covers about 20% of expenses. No current oil donor is documented.
records_note: Its Financial Reporting page posts annual reports from 1998 to 2025, audited statements from 2013 and Form 990s, plus a 2022-23 donor list.

name: Mediamatic
funding: Mondriaan Fund, Amsterdam Fund for the Arts (AFK), Creative Europe; non-profit foundation.

name: Medrar for Contemporary Art
funding: Space set up with support from Young Arab Theatre Fund, Foundation for Arts Initiatives, Abbara, Roberto Cimetta Fund, Netherlands Embassy in Cairo and AFAC through a Swiss SDC grant.
watch: Artist collective since 2005; runs the Cairo Video Festival. AFAC lists a 2019 North Africa Cultural Program grant. No current budget is published.
records_note: Names its founding supporters in one undated About sentence and lists no board; it publishes no annual reports or accounts.

name: MeetFactory
funding: Ministry of Culture Czech Republic, City of Prague, Creative Europe; independent non-profit cultural institution.

name: Mercer Union
funding: Canada Council, Ontario Arts Council, Toronto Arts Council. TD Bank Group leads support for a communications post; Burdock Brewery is beverage sponsor.
watch: TD Bank pleaded guilty in October 2024 to money-laundering conspiracy and Bank Secrecy Act failures, paying about $3B.
records_note: Names about 35 donors, three funders and its sponsors, lists an 11-member board and posts its 2024-25 impact report, but no financial statements.

name: Metropolitan Museum of Manila
funding: Formerly central-bank subsidised; now a non-profit foundation (1979, Imelda Marcos, Bienvenido Tantoco Sr.). Founding benefactors include Campos family firms NutriAsia and Del Monte Philippines; Metrobank and NCCA back programmes.
watch: NutriAsia, named a benefactor in 2021, saw police break up its 2018 Marilao strike: at least 30 people injured, 19 arrested.
records_note: Its site describes a non-government, not-for-profit foundation and posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; no Philippine register was readable.

name: MGLC International Centre of Graphic Arts
funding: Funded by the City of Ljubljana; organises the Ljubljana Biennale of Graphic Arts.
records_note: It lists its Board of Trustees and a founding-supporters roll from its creation, posts no annual reports, and its AJPES filings were not opened.

name: MIMA
funding: Teesside University unit. 2024-25 funders: Arts Council England, Middlesbrough Council, Freelands Foundation, Contemporary Art Society, Henry Moore Foundation, AHRC, Art Fund, Holiday Action Fund.
watch: Roster from the 2024-25 impact report. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: A Teesside University unit: one impact report (2024-25) names funders; the university publishes accounts 2002 to 2025 and lists its governors.

name: MO Museum
funding: Private museum founded by Danguolė and Viktoras Butkus (biotech).
records_note: MO posts annual reports for 2018-19 to 2025, names its patrons and partners on an undated page, and lists an advisory board, but no accounts.

name: MOCA Los Angeles
watch: Steven Cohen is no longer a trustee: the 2026-27 board roster omits him. The pin's controversy does not concern a current board figure.
records_note: Its site posts a Form 990 for the year to June 2025 and a 2026-27 board of 24 trustees, but no annual report or donors.

name: MOCA Taipei
funding: Owned by Taipei City, run by the Taipei Culture Foundation since 2008. Sponsors: Epson Taiwan, Lord Hotels, Contemporary Art Foundation, Sony, Thermos; five more logos unnamed.
watch: In 2020-21 director Lo Li-chen cancelled Jun Yang's show, then it was shortened after he threatened legal action. Taipei Times did not call it censorship.
records_note: The support page shows five undated sponsor logos with no alt text; no annual reports, accounts or board list found.
